decisions_log.summary: Measured the over-assignment, then hit a blocking finding the plan did not anticipate.
decisions_log.over_assignment: 2,445 of 2,778 elements carry imports; 11,578 entries attached; in ALL 203 files that have imports every element carries a byte-identical copy of the whole-file list.
decisions_log.measured_consequence: clones.ts:247 triviality: 193 elements qualify today, 1,264 would qualify under per-element imports. 1,071 elements are wrongly excluded - a live wrong answer, 6.5x.
decisions_log.blocking_finding: element.imports[].specifiers/.default/.namespace are NEVER populated. relationship-extractor.ts:1106 looks up import_clause via childForFieldName, which tree-sitter-typescript returns NULL for; the raw-facts path at :467 already works around exactly this and documents it in a comment. The block at :1120-1144 is dead code. Proven at grammar level on identical source.
decisions_log.consequence_for_the_plan: P1-T3 cannot pick the planned narrowing rule: matching an element body against import specifiers requires specifiers, and there are none. HALTING to report per P1-T3 rather than silently re-scoping the phase.

decisions_log.why_a_ruling_was_needed: The measured baseline showed the planned rule was unimplementable: there are no specifiers to match against. Options were put to the operator rather than re-scoped silently.
decisions_log.rule: keep an import on an element when any bound local name appears as a whole word in the element body span
decisions_log.error_asymmetry: false keep = harmless (status quo); false drop = data loss. Rule errs toward keeping.
decisions_log.honest_limit: text heuristic, not symbol resolution - comments/strings can cause a false keep, dynamic access can cause a false drop

decisions_log.summary: Phase 1 complete. The repair turned out to be THREE instances of one lookup defect, not one.
decisions_log.what_widened: P1-T6 first ran 8/10 green: specifiers worked but default and namespace did not. Same root cause one level deeper - childForFieldName("name") also returns null for the default binding and the namespace alias. Fixed by mirroring extractRawImports:494-499 and :515-522 rather than inventing a third approach.
decisions_log.revert_proof: 8/10 fail at HEAD; the 2 passers are the conservatism guards, which is the correct shape.
decisions_log.suite: 2637 -> 2647 passed, 33 skipped, zero regressions. populate-cli.test.ts fails identically before and after (pre-existing beforeAll tsc hook timeout).

decisions_log.detail: plan/inventory digest changed since alignment - expected, phase 1 edited plan.json. Advisory and non-blocking per the WARN-first contract; execution proceeds. Also required --allow-domain-mismatch to run at all, the known cross-project catch-22.

decisions_log.summary: Phase 2 placeholder replaced with 10 tasks; the phase-planning hard stop is now satisfied.
decisions_log.hard_stop_disposition: approved - gate satisfied by authoring the plan, NOT bypassed. No --bypass-hard-stops flag was passed.
decisions_log.scope: Collapse the last inline CODEREF_RAG_LOCAL_ONLY predicate (rag-search.ts:313-315) onto the canonical isLocalOnly(). Drift-risk removal, not a live-defect fix.
decisions_log.built_in_halt: P2-T3 halts for an operator ruling if the collapsed guard turns out to be unreachable by any test - the same halt shape that fired at P1-T3.

decisions_log.predicate_equivalence: CONFIRMED identical - 0 divergent guard outcomes across 22 inputs. Two return-type differences (undefined / "" vs strict false) that the `if (localOnly && ...)` consumer cannot observe.
decisions_log.reachability: The guard is LIVE (published bin, main() runs on every invocation, no in-repo spawner) but STRUCTURALLY UNTESTABLE: rag-search.ts has zero exports and calls main() unconditionally at module load.
decisions_log.sibling_divergence: rag-index, rag-status and rag-eval all guard main() behind require.main === module and export their surface. rag-search is the only one of the four rag-* CLIs that does not.
decisions_log.consequence_for_the_plan: P2-T3 HALT fires. The collapse is safe and provable-identical, but on its own it produces a change no test can reach. Making the module testable is a module-contract change beyond the stub scope, so it goes to the operator by name rather than being absorbed silently.

decisions_log.ruling: (A) collapse AND mirror the sibling convention
decisions_log.rationale: rag-index/rag-status/rag-eval already guard main() behind require.main === module and export their surface; rag-search was the only one of the four rag-* CLIs that did not. Mirroring the family beats inventing a second convention, and it is what makes the collapse provable.

decisions_log.summary: Phase 2 complete. The predicate collapse was inert as measured; the load-bearing change is that the seam is now reachable.
decisions_log.revert_proof: 21/21 fail at HEAD, and the failure is process.exit fired from main() during the import - the structural defect demonstrating itself.

decisions_log.surface: No observable behaviour change. Verified end-to-end against the built bin: --help still works, local-only + openai still exits 2 with the identical message, and ollama still passes the guard.
decisions_log.honest_note: populate-cli.test.ts passing this run is a timing artefact of the preceding tsc warm-up, NOT a repair by this phase.
